org: Humanitarian Data Exchange (UN OCHA Centre for Humanitarian Data)
accessNotes: data.humdata.org/dataviz-guide/* now returns 404. The guide was a Frontify guideline; the Frontify share link (company-200741.frontify.com/d/1GC9otcJfhPe) renders only the home page (links back to the dead humdata URLs) and the portal requires login. A 2024 Wayback capture of /dataviz-elements/ contains only the Frontify sidebar (section list: Text/Key figures styles, Bar charts vertical vs horizontal, stacked, 100% stacked, Line charts single/multiple/small multiples, Area, Pie, Donut, Bubble, Sparklines, Matrix tables, Tables/date format, Icons/IcoMoon); content is JS-loaded and Wayback was intermittently offline. Primary substitute: OCHA-DAP's own gghdx R package, which explicitly implements 'the HDX visual guidelines' (colour ramps cite data.humdata.org/dataviz-guide/visual-identity/#/visual-identity/colours) and ships the two reference images 'from the original visual guide' (covid_blue.png, covid_red.png). Values below for the legacy (guide-era) design come from gghdx's legacy theme/palette; 2025-redesign values are noted separately.
summary: HDX's data-viz style is a clean humanitarian web/report style: bold dark left-aligned headline, a one-line source/date strip directly under the title ('DATA | date | Source' with 'DATA' in HDX blue), light grey horizontal gridlines, no y-axis line, grey uppercase axis labels, and data drawn in flat HDX 'sapphire' blue. Emphasis is created by tinting all bars in an ultra-light ramp tone and colouring the key bar in the full-strength hue (tomato red). Numbers are abbreviated with uppercase K/M/B.

colors.categoricalNotes: Legacy (guide-era) discrete scale from gghdx hdx_pal_discrete(design='legacy'): count-specific — n=1: mint-hdx #1EBFB3; n=2: mint #1EBFB3, sapphire #007CE0; n=3: mint, sapphire, tomato #F2645A; n=4: sapphire, mint, tomato, mint-light #78D9D1; n=5 adds tomato-light #F7A29C; n=6 adds sapphire-light #66B0EC; n=7 adds tomato-dark #C25048; n=8 adds sapphire-dark #0063B3; ... max 12. 'tomato used only when necessary for odd # of colors'. Each hue is a 4-step ramp dark/hdx/light/ultra-light: sapphire #0063B3/#007CE0/#66B0EC/#CCE5F9; mint #18998F/#1EBFB3/#78D9D1/#D2F2F0; tomato #C25048/#F2645A/#F7A29C/#FCE0DE. 2025 redesign: primary-5 #1862D8, brand-5 #269777, error-5 #C44536 (n=1 brand-5; n=2 brand-5, primary-5; n=3 + error-5; n>=4 primary-5, brand-5, error-5, brand-3 #7DC1AD, error-3 #DC8F86, primary-3 #74A1E8, error-7 #762920, primary-7 #0E3B82, brand-7 #18614C ...).
colors.notes: Legacy grays: black #000000, dark #888888, medium #CCCCCC, light #EEEEEE, white #FFFFFF; gghdx legacy theme uses gray-light #EEEEEE for gridlines and gray-dark #888888 for axis line/text. Sampled from the guide's reference image covid_blue.png: bars #037BE0 (≈ sapphire #007CE0), title #333333, axis labels/source #888888, gridlines #EEEEEE. In covid_red.png the context bars are tomato ultra-light #FCE0DE and the highlighted last bar tomato #F2645A. 2025 redesign neutral ramp: neutral-2 #D8E0E1 (gridlines/axis), neutral-5 #9DB1B3 (axis text), neutral-8 #3F4748 (body text), neutral-95 #101212 (titles); bars default primary-4 #4681E0, lines/points primary-5 #1862D8. Status ramps: success-5 #2F9E6F, warning-5 #D48F2A, error-5 #C44536.

typography.family: Source Sans Pro (Source Sans 3) — guide era; 2025 redesign: Roboto body + Merriweather titles

axisTitle.placement: usually omitted in reference charts (x = '', y = ''); when present y title rotated 90°

source.style: normal; 'DATA' keyword in HDX blue, then ' | date | Source org' in grey

typography.notes: Sizes are gghdx relative sizes for base_size 10: title rel 1.5 (15), subtitle rel 1.1 (11), axis text rel 1 (10), axis title rel 1.25, legend title rel 1.25, strip text rel 1.1 bold. Month labels uppercase 3-letter ('JAN', 'FEB'). Guide section 'Key figures styles' exists (big-number key figures) but content not retrievable.

structure.gridlines: Horizontal major gridlines only (#EEEEEE, solid, thin) for vertical bar/line charts; vertical-only for horizontal bars (gghdx horizontal=FALSE removes y grid). No minor gridlines.
structure.axisLine: No y-axis line (axis.line.y blank). x-axis baseline drawn thin grey.
structure.ticks: Legacy: no tick marks (axis.ticks blank). 2025: light neutral-2 ticks.
structure.zeroLine: Data starts exactly at the axis — scale_y_continuous_hdx sets expand = c(0,0) so bars sit on the baseline with no padding.
structure.yAxisTitle: omitted; measure stated in the title
structure.unitPlacement: In tick labels via abbreviations (500K, 1.0M, 2.0M) and in the title.
structure.frame: none (panel.border blank, white plot and panel)
structure.notes: Plot margins 12/10/12/10 pt; title positioned relative to the whole plot (plot.title.position = 'plot'), i.e. flush left with the y-axis labels.

marks.bars: Flat solid bars, no outline, no rounding; narrow bars with clear gaps in time series (reference ≈60% bar width). Guide sections distinguish vertical vs horizontal bars, stacked and 100% stacked.
marks.lines: Default line colour primary blue; guide covers single, multiple-line and small-multiple line charts.
marks.areas: Single, multiple and stacked area charts plus small multiples (guide sections).
marks.points: Default point colour primary blue, gghdx size rel 2.
marks.pies: Pie and donut sections exist in the guide (allowed); detailed rules not retrievable.
marks.notes: Bubble charts: single-colour bubbles, combination with line chart, log scale, 'let the user decide'. Sparklines and matrix tables also covered.

labels.numberFormat: label_number_hdx: numbers ≥1,000 → X.YK; ≥10,000 → XYK; ≥100,000 → XYZK; same for M and B (and T); uppercase suffix; ticks show one decimal for M (1.0M, 1.5M, 2.0M); negatives handled; prefix e.g. -$1.1K. Not used for percentages.
labels.dates: Uppercase three-letter month abbreviations on axes (JAN, FEB…); source strip date as 'DD MON YYYY' uppercase (e.g. '28 SEP 2020'). Guide has a Table 'Date format' section.
labels.notes: Guide 'Text' section covers number formatting (referenced by gghdx label_number_hdx docs).

furniture.title: Bold, dark (#333333) left-aligned headline, can be a finding ('Monthly global COVID-19 number of cases surpasses two million'), wraps to two lines.
furniture.source: Directly under the title, before the plot: 'DATA | 28 SEP 2020 | World Health Organization' — the word 'DATA' in HDX blue, separators and rest in grey #888888, regular weight.
furniture.other: No border, no footer in reference charts.

annotations: Highlight by colour: all bars in ultra-light tint (#FCE0DE) and the emphasised bar in full tomato (#F2645A).
layout: Reference images are small web widgets (~367×318 px). Small multiples are recommended for multiple lines/areas.
accessibility: Each colour ramp step designed for contrast; no further detail recoverable.

chartTypes.notes: Guide has Do/Don't pages for text, bars, lines and tables (not retrievable).

distinctiveRules.rule: Source/date strip sits directly under the title (above the plot), formatted 'DATA | DD MON YYYY | Source' with 'DATA' in HDX blue and the rest grey.
distinctiveRules.quote: Reference image from the original visual guide: 'DATA | 28 SEP 2020 | World Health Organization'

distinctiveRules.rule: Title is bold, dark grey (#333333), left-aligned flush with the y-axis labels (plot-level title position).
distinctiveRules.quote: plot.title: size rel(1.5), hjust = 0, face = 'bold'; plot.title.position = 'plot'

distinctiveRules.rule: Only horizontal light-grey (#EEEEEE) gridlines for column/line charts; flipped to vertical-only for horizontal bars; no minor gridlines.
distinctiveRules.quote: panel.grid.major color gray-light; if (horizontal) panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()

distinctiveRules.rule: No y-axis line and no tick marks.
Data starts exactly on the x-axis (no padding below zero).
distinctiveRules.quote: scale_y_continuous_hdx() wraps scale_y_continuous() to plot data directly starting from the y-axis ... sets expand = c(0, 0)

distinctiveRules.rule: Abbreviate numbers with uppercase K/M/B suffixes (500K, 1.5M, 2.0M).
distinctiveRules.quote: numbers 1,000 and above to X.YK, 10,000 and above to XYK ... replacing the K with an M, and the same for B

distinctiveRules.rule: Month axis labels are uppercase three-letter abbreviations in grey (JAN, FEB, MAR).
Single-series default colour is HDX sapphire blue #007CE0 (legacy) / primary blue (2025).
Highlight pattern: context marks in the ultra-light tint of a ramp, emphasised mark in the full-strength hue of the same ramp.
distinctiveRules.quote: Reference image: pale #FCE0DE bars with final bar in tomato #F2645A

distinctiveRules.rule: Categorical palette is count-specific: 1→mint, 2→mint+sapphire, 3→mint+sapphire+tomato, then light/dark ramp steps; tomato only for odd counts; max 12.
distinctiveRules.quote: hdx_pal_discrete_legacy ... tomato used only when necessary for odd # of colors

distinctiveRules.rule: Legend at the bottom, centred, no key background.

referenceImages.describes: Reference chart from the original HDX visual guide. Bold dark-grey sans-serif title top-left on two lines 'Monthly global COVID-19 confirmed cases in 2020'. Directly beneath: 'DATA | 28 SEP 2020 | World Health Organization' with 'DATA' in blue, the rest grey. Narrow solid blue (#037BE0) columns, one per week, with gaps. Light grey horizontal gridlines; y labels on the left in grey: 0.0, 500K, 1.0M, 1.5M, 2.0M; no y-axis line or ticks; x-axis uppercase month labels JAN..SEP in grey. No legend, no logo, white background.

Same layout with headline-as-finding 'Monthly global COVID-19 number of cases surpasses two million'. All columns are very pale pink (#FCE0DE) except the final column in solid tomato red (#F2645A), illustrating highlight-one-bar emphasis. Same 'DATA | date | source' strip and grey axes/gridlines.

gghdx (2025 design) recreation: large bold Merriweather serif title and bold serif 'DATA | JUL 2022 | World Health Organization' subtitle in near-black; blue (#007CE0-like) narrow columns; pale blue-grey horizontal gridlines; grey-teal Roboto axis labels (0, 2M, 4M...) on the left with no y-axis line; uppercase month labels with small ticks on a light baseline. Shows the redesign's typography.
